claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Section heading printed in the PDF is transcribed as a plain paragraph with no Markdown heading marker, so it is lost from the document outline; should be '### 7.3.3 Paragraph Header, Paragraph-Name, and Paragraph' (siblings such as 7.2.4 / 7.2 carry headings).

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page (folio IV-43) prints '7.3.3 Paragraph Header, Paragraph-Name, and Paragraph' as a bold numbered clause heading on its own line, followed by its body text. page-189.md and specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 7862 carry it as a plain paragraph with no '#' marker, while the same chapter's siblings in specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md are headings ('## 7.2 REFERENCE FORMAT REPRESENTATION' at line 7776, '### 7.2.4 Comment Lines' at line 7834). So the clause is missing from the outline. Under that scheme, '### 7.3.3' is the right level. The text itself is transcribed correctly; only the heading marker is missing. The same defect also covers 7.2.5, 7.3, 7.3.1, 7.3.2 and 7.4 on this page, which presumably have their own claims.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as stated: 7.3.3 is printed as a numbered clause heading but transcribed as plain text with no Markdown heading marker; it should be '### 7.3.3 Paragraph Header, Paragraph-Name, and Paragraph' (with '## 7.3 ...' as its parent).
